notes: Twelve weave pairs linking the raiders, veterans, air groups and swarm-minds that had no authored ties yet.

C.title: Same Look
beats: Marlow and Wren come out of the creek laughing. Cinder Hook is already kneeling at the gate, planting something.
We were going to surprise them.
I was going to surprise you first.

B.title: Who Goes First
beats: The Marauders arrived before the warning. Cinder Hook's Trappers had arrived before the Marauders.
Someone has to be. Mind the third step.

A.title: Cousins
beats: The raid went off like a joke with a long setup. Nobody on the enemy side got the punchline in time.
We don't apologise, you know. To anyone.
Neither do I. I just leave notes in the dirt.
Leave one for us. We'll read it on the way out.

C.title: Wet Welder
beats: Twitcher is bolting something to the gate when the Marauders drip past him, still laughing.
You're building. Both of us look guilty.
I'm always building. Guilt is a separate project.

B.title: Spare Parts
beats: Twitcher has welded a tow hook to the Marauders' hull. They have not asked why, and they have not removed it.
It's a good hook for a bad idea. Come see.

A.title: The Bridge That Wasn't
beats: Twitcher laid a bridge over the ford at midnight. The Marauders took it at dawn, and the enemy took the river.
I never said it would hold a crowd.
It held us. Everyone else was late.

C.title: Whose Water
beats: Six Cutlasses sit on the bend. The Marauders come out of it from underneath.
Mind your floats. This is our river.
Your river has my wing on it.
Then your wing is parked in our front garden.

B.title: Right of Way
beats: A flooded crossing, two ways through it, and no one willing to wait for the other.
I land. You drive. Same crossing.
You got there wet. I got there with a view.

A.title: Shared Current
beats: The Cutlasses held the sky over the bend while Marlow and Wren came up through the reeds. The defenders watched the wrong one.
Half is generous. I'll fly over the other half.

motifs: the hero with the big gun

C.title: Where It Hurts
beats: Halbard is polishing a heat ray the size of a cart. Ferrow looks at it the way a man looks at weather.
I'm sure. I'm still standing a hundred feet behind you when you fire it.

B.title: A Door With Sense
beats: Ferrow walks the Halberd around the camp, pointing at the places a door tends to get hit.
Rear plate. Left hinge. The bit nobody thinks about.
Every one of them has a story. I kept the receipts.

A.title: Take the Hit
beats: The ray sang across the field. The return fire found the Lunkhead, who had already moved into it.
You stepped in front of me.
I stepped where it was going to hurt anyway. Different thing.
I'll fire twice as slow. For you.

motifs: the veteran and the shield counterpart
the left side of the line

C.title: Same Dirt
beats: Pavise is oiling her Centurion's plate. Ferrow parks his Lunkhead beside it without being asked.
You knew the commander before the suit changed.
I just woke up in the company. It felt right.

B.title: Two Old Walls
beats: They hold the gate together, one with a ward and one with receipts.
You wait for it to hurt.
You wait for it to arrive. Both ways work.

A.title: Every Warrior
beats: The ward still remembers every Warrior that stood in that dirt. Ferrow finally asks to hear the names.
I've kept the injuries. Never learned the names.
Then we trade. I'll give you the names.
And I'll tell you which of them it hurt.

motifs: a veteran who has seen it all
a pack that is one thought

C.title: One Mind, One Wall
beats: Vane's twelve Phobos peel off the line together. Ferrow watches them go without turning his head.
Mine stays. That's the difference between us.

B.title: Rhythm and Receipt
beats: Vane counts the beat aloud. Ferrow counts something else under his breath.
I'm keeping score. It runs slower than a rhythm.
It runs later. Mine runs first.

A.title: The Hold
beats: The beat broke under heavy laser fire. The pack scattered, and the only thing still standing was one grey plod.
Your wall held when my rhythm didn't.
A wall is a very short thought. But it survives.
Teach my flock one. Just one.

motifs: a dropship with its own sky

C.title: Whose Altitude
beats: Reeve and Noctua both file flight paths for the same valley. The charts overlap like a bad argument.
I dream mine. It's less crowded.

B.title: Lane Dispute
beats: The Highwinds ran into the drone cloud over the ridge. Both groups broke and re-formed within ten seconds.
I flew over it. The altitude was free.

A.title: Two Skies
beats: Noctua's drones carpeted the radar while the Stronghold set down in the hole they left. No one dropped a single plane.
I'll keep to it. Next time I may even file.
I'll believe it when I see it on paper.

motifs: never looking at what she hits

C.title: Flight Plan
beats: Reeve hands Thresh a drop zone marked in red. Thresh looks at the sky above it and nothing else.

B.title: Timing
beats: The Hailstorm cleared the zone with a minute to spare. The Stronghold needed ninety seconds.
I'm always fast. I just don't look at what I hit.
I do. Mine have to walk through it.

A.title: Bombs Away, Boots Down
beats: For once Thresh waited. The ship set down in the quiet where the bombs had been, and every passenger stepped out alive.
Full of your people. I'll not do that again.

motifs: a flock that moves as one

C.title: Landing Pattern
beats: Vane's Phobos peel up the slope in one motion. Reeve watches them from the open ramp of the Stronghold.
I could put you down where you're needed.
I could be there before you land.

B.title: Same Beat
beats: Highwinds, Banshees and Phobos moved across the field on one rhythm. Nobody had agreed to it.
Close enough is how a swarm begins.

A.title: Drop Zone
beats: The Stronghold set down in the middle of the enemy line. The flock was already waiting there, as if it had always lived in that field.
You beat me to my own landing.
I heard you coming. It was the best note of the day.

motifs: seven Possums and a pile of Ticks

C.title: Count Them
beats: Pip counts seven hovers. Tamsin counts twenty fleas and gives up at the number.

B.title: Cheap Is Quick
beats: Both packs lost a third of their number on the same sortie. Both laughed about it afterwards.
We played dead cheap. It costs the same.

A.title: Plurals
beats: The two swarms covered the fog together, hovers above and fleas below. The enemy radar stopped counting.
We are the eyes with rockets. Don't tell the singular ones.
We never speak to the singular ones.

C.title: Wheels or Rockets
beats: Spoke's Wheelie Bay rolls out sixteen scouts. Pip lets his Seekers hover quietly overhead.
Floating doesn't get a tyre punctured.
Both of us are about to find out.

B.title: Whose Map
beats: The Wheelies and the Seekers reported on the same hill. They gave two different answers.
Then yours is the nervous kind.

A.title: Eyes Agree
beats: For one afternoon the Wheelies and the Seekers drew the same map. They did not mention it to each other.
Fine. You see well for something that floats.
You see well for something on wheels.

C.title: Playing Dead
beats: The Possums lie still in the grass. The Infestor seed stands in the same patch, and there are now six of them.
Mine plays dead. That's half the trick. Yours is just showing off.

B.title: Stillness
beats: Both packs waited in the same hollow for the enemy to pass. One pretended to be empty. The other was quietly adding to itself.
You'll want to move over. I'm planting.

A.title: Ready or Not
beats: Seven Possums stood up on cue. The hive had already put a dozen more behind them.
I didn't ask for the help.
Nobody asks. They simply become the company.
Then I'll grudgingly say thank you.
